label: 道 · 無
title: 道 ↔ 無 · The Nameless Source
subtitle: Classical usage
evidence: The Daodejing ties the Way to non-presence: the nameless (無名) is the beginning of heaven and earth (ch. 1), and being is born from non-being (ch. 40). 道 is the course; 無 is the openness it runs through.

label: 無為
title: 無為 · wúwéi
subtitle: A Daoist term, repurposed by Buddhist translators
evidence: “Without” + “action”: in Daoist texts, efficacy that does not force; in Buddhist translation, the unconditioned (asaṃskṛta) as opposed to the conditioned (有為). The same two characters carry both histories.

label: 無量
title: 無量 · wúliàng
subtitle: Attested translation of apramāṇa
evidence: “Without” + “measure” renders Sanskrit apramāṇa: the boundless scope of loving-kindness, compassion, sympathetic joy and equanimity (maitrī, karuṇā, muditā, upekṣā).

label: 不二
title: 不二 · bú èr · advaya
subtitle: Attested translation — the bridge at the centre
evidence: “Not” + “two” renders Sanskrit advaya, non-duality: the refusal to split reality into opposed pairs. In the galaxy, 不 and 二 sit in the two eyes of the attractor — two foci, one trajectory.
caveat: Zhuangzi’s “pivot of the Way” (道樞) is an earlier Chinese parallel, not a source of the compound (see 二).

label: 量 · 司
title: 量 ↔ 司 · Measured Stewardship
subtitle: Original interpretation
evidence: Proposed pairing: stewardship (司) guided by measure (量) — direction grounded in valid knowing and a sense of proportion rather than force.
caveat: No classical compound joins these two characters; the connection is the project’s own.
statusNote: Ben to confirm whether this proposition is his to keep.

label: 道生一
title: 道 → 一 · The Way Gives Rise to the One
subtitle: Daodejing ch. 42
evidence: Ch. 42 opens: 道生一，一生二，二生三，三生萬物 — “the Way gives rise to one, one to two, two to three, three to the myriad things.” The Shuowen’s first entry echoes it: 道立於一, “the Way was established in the One”.
caveat: What “one”, “two” and “three” stand for is a commentators’ question (qi; yin and yang; their harmony are common answers). The text itself does not say.
gaps: Open Daodejing ch. 42 in a reliable edition and record the passage.

label: 一生二
title: 一 → 二 · One Gives Rise to Two
subtitle: Daodejing ch. 42
evidence: The same sentence continues: 一生二, “one gives rise to two”. This is the first documented link between 二 and anything in the other half of the Pillars: through 一, 不 二 愛 and 道 無 為 量 司 are now joined.
caveat: The Daodejing’s two is a cosmogonic two; the Pillars’ 二 is mainly about 不二 (advaya). The bridge joins the characters, not those doctrines, and not-two is not one (see 二’s card, Advaya ≠ Advaita).
gaps: Open Daodejing ch. 42 in a reliable edition and record the passage.

label: 有無相生
title: 有 ↔ 無 · Being and Non-Being Arise Together
subtitle: Daodejing chs. 2 and 40
evidence: Being and non-being give rise to each other (有無相生, ch. 2); “the myriad things are born from being, and being is born from non-being” (天下萬物生於有，有生於無, ch. 40). 無 here is not nihilistic nothing but the indeterminate source of form.

checked.edition: https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/49965 (B. R. Linnell, Dao De Jing: A Minimalist Translation, 2015; Wang Bi text with variants)

label: 名可名
title: 道 ↔ 名 · The Way That Can Be Told, the Name That Can Be Named
subtitle: Daodejing ch. 1
evidence: The Daodejing opens with the pair: 道可道，非常道；名可名，非常名 — “a way that can be told is not the constant Way; a name that can be named is not the constant name.” Way and name stand side by side from the first line.

checked.edition: https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/49965 (B. R. Linnell, Dao De Jing: A Minimalist Translation, 2015; Wang Bi text with variants)
checked.note: 道可道非常道 · 名可名非常名

label: 道法自然
title: 法 ↔ 道 · Each Takes the Next as Its Model
subtitle: Daodejing ch. 25
evidence: 人法地，地法天，天法道，道法自然: humans take Earth as their model, Earth takes Heaven, Heaven takes the Way, and the Way “takes as its model what is so of itself”. 法 is the verb in every step. 自然 here is not Nature as a thing but the unforced way things go: 道 imitates nothing outside itself.
caveat: The last two sentences were accepted as 道’s satellite 道法自然 (folded into this bridge on 2026-11-04); the chain sentence is Baracus’s addition and awaits acceptance.

checked.note: 道法自然 (partial edition, simplified script)

label: 四無量心
title: 慈 ↔ 量 · The First of the Four Immeasurables
subtitle: Buddhist translation
evidence: The four immeasurables (apramāṇa, 四無量心) are 慈 悲 喜 捨: loving-kindness, compassion, sympathetic joy and equanimity, “immeasurable” because they extend to beings without limit. 慈 is the first; 量 supplies the measure that 無 negates.

cites.locator: ch. 8 分別定品: 四無量

label: 慈 · 愛
title: 慈 ↔ 愛 · Glossed as One, Translated Apart
subtitle: Shuowen; Buddhist translation
evidence: The Shuowen glosses 慈 with 愛: 慈，愛也. Buddhist translation pulled the two apart: 慈 became maitrī, loving-kindness, and 愛 became tṛṣṇā, craving, a cause of suffering in the twelve links (see 愛’s card).
caveat: In ordinary Chinese the two still overlap, as in 慈愛, “tender love”. The distinction is the translators’ convention, not a change in the everyday words.

label: 心 · 愛
title: 心 ↔ 愛 · The Heart Inside Love
subtitle: Graphic structure
evidence: Mojidata IDS describes 愛 as 爫 over 冖 over 𢖻, and 𢖻 as 心 over 夊: the heart is a component, at the centre of the graph. The simplified 爱 replaces it with 友, the subject of the joke on 愛’s card.

label: 中道
title: 空 ↔ 道 · Emptiness Is the Middle Way
subtitle: Mūlamadhyamakakārikā 24.18, tr. Kumārajīva
evidence: Kumārajīva’s rendering of Nāgārjuna’s verse 24.18 ends 亦是中道義, “this is also the meaning of the Middle Way”: dependent arising, emptiness, provisional naming and the Middle Way (madhyamā pratipad, 中道) are given as one. 道 here renders pratipad, a path, as on 道’s card (mārga).
caveat: Baracus recalls that the Taishō text of T1564 reads 我說即是無 where later Chinese tradition (from Tiantai) quotes 我說即是空. If so, the verse joins 空 to the Middle Way through the received sense, and also touches 無. Check before accepting.
gaps: Open T1564 at verse 24.18 on CBETA and record whether the Taishō text reads 我說即是無 or 我說即是空.

label: 假名
title: 空 ↔ 名 · Empty, and So a Provisional Name
subtitle: Mūlamadhyamakakārikā 24.18, tr. Kumārajīva
evidence: The same verse: what arises from conditions is empty, and 亦為是假名, “it is a provisional name” (prajñapti). Things are named and the names work, but nothing answers to them as an independent thing.
gaps: Open T1564 at verse 24.18 on CBETA and record whether the Taishō text reads 我說即是無 or 我說即是空.

label: 心 · 慈
title: 心 ↔ 慈 · Kindness Has a Heart at Its Foot
subtitle: Graphic structure
evidence: Mojidata IDS: 慈 is 兹 over 心. The Shuowen reads it the same way: 从心，茲聲, the heart for meaning and 茲 for sound.

label: 心 · 悲
title: 心 ↔ 悲 · Grief Has a Heart at Its Foot
subtitle: Graphic structure
evidence: Mojidata IDS: 悲 is 非 over 心. The Shuowen: 从心，非聲, the heart for meaning and 非 for sound.
caveat: Reading 悲 as “not-heart” is folk etymology: 非 is phonetic here.

label: 慈悲
title: 慈 ↔ 悲 · Kindness and Compassion
subtitle: Buddhist translation
evidence: 慈悲 joins the first two immeasurables, maitrī and karuṇā, and became the everyday Chinese word for Buddhist compassion as a whole.
caveat: The familiar formula 慈能與樂，悲能拔苦 (“kindness gives happiness, compassion removes suffering”) is usually traced to the 大智度論 (T1509), which is not yet a registered source.

cites.locator: ch. 8 分別定品: 四無量

gaps: Register T1509 (大智度論) and cite the 與樂拔苦 passage.

label: 如實
title: 如 ↔ 實 · As It Really Is
subtitle: yathābhūta
evidence: 如實 renders Sanskrit yathābhūta, “as it has come to be”: yathā, “as”, for 如, and bhūta, “what has become, what is”, for 實. 如實知見, knowing and seeing as it really is, recurs throughout the Āgamas. It is this project’s name.

label: 真言
title: 真 ↔ 言 · The True Word
subtitle: mantra; Japanese shingon
evidence: 真言, “true word”, renders mantra. In Japan the Shingon school (真言宗), founded by Kūkai, is named for it; Unihan’s Japanese readings give 真 shin and 言 gon, hence shingon.

checked.note: 真 SHIN · 言 GEN GON

label: 真如
title: 真 ↔ 如 · True Suchness
subtitle: tathatā
evidence: 真如, “true suchness”, renders tathatā, the way things are before they are named. Kumārajīva often wrote 如 or 如如 alone; 真如 became the standard term in later translation.
caveat: The history of the renderings is Baracus’s, from general knowledge; check it against the translations before accepting.
gaps: Cite where 真如 first becomes standard (e.g. Xuanzang’s translations).

label: 真實
title: 真 ↔ 實 · True, and Not False
subtitle: Heart Sutra
evidence: The Heart Sutra says its mantra 能除一切苦，真實不虛: “it removes all suffering, true and not false.” 真實 joins the two words for “true”: 真, the genuine as against the counterfeit, and 實, the solid as against the empty.

label: 符 · 印
title: 符 ↔ 印 · Tally and Seal
subtitle: Shuowen
evidence: The Shuowen glosses both with 信, “credence, proof”: 符，信也, and 印，執政所持信也. A tally proves by fitting, a seal by its mark; both make a message trustworthy, and both point toward 信.

label: 名 · 實
title: 名 ↔ 實 · The Name Is the Guest of Reality
subtitle: Zhuangzi ch. 1
evidence: Zhuangzi ch. 1: declining the throne, Xu You says 名者，實之賓也 — “a name is the guest of reality.” The pair 名 / 實 (name and actuality) runs through early Chinese philosophy, and 實 is half of Rushi’s own name, 如實.

label: 名 · 言
title: 名 ↔ 言 · Rectifying Names
subtitle: Analects 13.3
evidence: Analects 13.3: 名不正，則言不順；言不順，則事不成 — “if names are not correct, speech does not accord with things; if speech does not accord, affairs do not succeed.” For Confucius, order begins with calling things what they are.

label: 無上咒
title: 咒 ↔ 無 · The Unsurpassed Mantra
subtitle: Heart Sutra
evidence: The Heart Sutra calls the perfection of wisdom 是大神咒，是大明咒，是無上咒，是無等等咒: a great spirit-mantra, a great knowledge-mantra, an unsurpassed mantra, an unequalled mantra. 無上 renders anuttara, “with nothing above”.

label: 虛心 · 實腹
title: 實 ↔ 心 · Empty the Heart, Fill the Belly
subtitle: Daodejing ch. 3
evidence: Ch. 3: 是以聖人之治，虛其心，實其腹 — “so the sage governs by emptying their hearts and filling their bellies.” 實 is a verb here, “to fill”, set against 虛, “to empty”; the heart is what is emptied.

label: 實相無相
title: 實 ↔ 無 · The True Mark Is No Mark
subtitle: Wumenguan case 6
evidence: In case 6 of the Wumenguan the Buddha holds up a flower, and says he entrusts to Mahākāśyapa 涅槃妙心，實相無相: “the wondrous mind of nirvāṇa, the true mark that is no mark.” Reality, in this line, is marked by having no mark.

label: 本無 → 如
title: 如 ↔ 無 · Suchness, Once Written as Non-Being
subtitle: Buddhist translation, Han to Tang
evidence: Lokakṣema rendered tathatā, “suchness”, as 本無, “original non-being”, in the Daoxing banruo jing (see 無’s card). Later translators wrote 如, “thus”, and 真如: the same idea moved from a word of absence to a word of likeness.
caveat: Lokakṣema’s 本無 is recorded on 無’s card; the later history of 如 is Baracus’s, from general knowledge.

label: λόγος → 道
title: 言 ↔ 道 · In the Beginning Was the Word
subtitle: John 1:1, Chinese Union Version
evidence: The Chinese Union Version (1919) opens the Gospel of John: 太初有道，道與神同在，道就是神. Greek λόγος means first “word, speech, account”, closest to 言, but the translators chose 道, which also means “to say”, as in 道可道.
caveat: Baracus recalls that Robert Morrison’s earlier translation (1823) used 言 here; check before citing it.

label: 負陰抱陽
title: 陰 ↔ 陽 · Carrying Yin, Embracing Yang
subtitle: Daodejing ch. 42
evidence: Ch. 42, after 道生一…三生萬物: 萬物負陰而抱陽，沖氣以為和 — “the myriad things carry yin on their backs and hold yang in their arms; blending qi, they make harmony.” The same chapter that opens with the Way giving rise to one.
gaps: Open Daodejing ch. 42 in a reliable edition and record the passage.

label: 輕清 · 重濁
title: 天 ↔ 地 · The Light Rose, the Heavy Settled
subtitle: Shuowen
evidence: The Shuowen’s entry for 地: 元气初分，輕清陽為天，重濁陰為地 — “when the primal qi first divided, the light and clear, yang, became Heaven; the heavy and turbid, yin, became Earth.” Heaven, Earth, yin, yang and qi in one sentence.

label: 三才
title: 天 ↔ 人 · The Three Powers
subtitle: Yijing, Shuogua
evidence: The Shuogua: 立天之道曰陰與陽，立地之道曰柔與剛，立人之道曰仁與義。兼三才而兩之 — “the way of Heaven is yin and yang, of Earth soft and hard, of the human humaneness and rightness; the three powers, each doubled.” Hence six lines to a hexagram.

label: 變通趣時
title: 易 ↔ 時 · Change Follows the Time
subtitle: Yijing, Xici
evidence: The Xici: 剛柔者，立本者也；變通者，趣時者也 — “the firm and the yielding set up the root; change and continuity follow the time.” To change well is to change in time.

label: 一陰一陽
title: 陽 ↔ 道 · One Yin, One Yang: That Is the Way
subtitle: Yijing, Xici
evidence: The Xici: 一陰一陽之謂道 — “one yin, one yang: that is called the Way.” Where the Daodejing says the Way cannot be told, the Xici gives it a rhythm: alternation itself.

label: 一 in 天
title: 天 ↔ 一 · One Over the Great
subtitle: Graphic structure
evidence: Mojidata IDS: 天 is 一 over 大. The Shuowen reads it the same way, 从一大: the stroke of one above the great person.

label: 仁者人也
title: 人 ↔ 仁 · Humaneness Is Being Human
subtitle: Mencius 7B16; graphic structure
evidence: Mencius 7B16: 仁也者，人也 — “humaneness is being human.” The two words are homophones (rén), and the graph of 仁 contains 人 (Mojidata IDS: ⿰亻二).

label: 克己復禮
title: 禮 ↔ 仁 · Returning to Ritual Is Humaneness
subtitle: Analects 12.1
evidence: Analects 12.1: 顏淵問仁。子曰：克己復禮為仁 — “Yan Yuan asked about humaneness. The Master said: to overcome oneself and return to ritual is humaneness.”

label: 為仁之本
title: 孝 ↔ 仁 · The Root of Humaneness
subtitle: Analects 1.2
evidence: Analects 1.2, Youzi: 孝弟也者，其為仁之本與 — “filial devotion and respect for elders: are they not the root of humaneness?”

label: 主忠信
title: 忠 ↔ 信 · Hold to Wholeheartedness and Good Faith
subtitle: Analects 1.8
evidence: Analects 1.8: 主忠信，無友不如己者，過則勿憚改 — “hold to wholeheartedness and good faith; … when you err, do not fear to change.” The pair recurs through the Analects.

label: 仁義 · nhân nghĩa
title: 仁 ↔ 義 · Humaneness and Rightness
subtitle: Mencius 1A1; Vietnam, 1428
evidence: Mencius opens by refusing profit: 王何必曰利？亦有仁義而已矣 — “why must the king speak of profit? There is humaneness and rightness, that is all.” In Vietnam, Nguyễn Trãi’s proclamation of 1428 begins 仁義之舉，要在安民, nhân nghĩa: “the work of humaneness and rightness lies in giving the people peace.”
caveat: The Unihan Vietnamese readings (nhân, nghĩa) are checked; the quotation from the Bình Ngô đại cáo is Baracus’s, from general knowledge.

label: 道生 · 德畜
title: 德 ↔ 道 · The Way Gives Birth, Virtue Rears
subtitle: Daodejing ch. 51
evidence: Ch. 51: 道生之，德畜之，物形之，勢成之 — “the Way gives them birth, virtue rears them, things give them shape, circumstance completes them.” The book is the classic of 道 and 德, and here is why they go together.

label: 愛人
title: 仁 ↔ 愛 · To Love People
subtitle: Analects 12.22
evidence: Analects 12.22: 樊遲問仁。子曰：「愛人。」 — “Fan Chi asked about humaneness. The Master said: love people.” The shortest definition of the central virtue is 愛.
caveat: The check recorded here is the one logged on 2026-11-04 in CORRECTIONS.md (ctext.org), made in support of 愛’s card.

label: 仁之端
title: 仁 ↔ 心 · The Sprout of Humaneness
subtitle: Mencius 2A6
evidence: Mencius 2A6: 人皆有不忍人之心 — “everyone has a heart that cannot bear the suffering of others” — and 惻隱之心，仁之端也, “the heart of compassion is the sprout of humaneness”. For Mencius the virtues begin in the heart as sprouts that must be grown.

label: 二 in 仁
title: 仁 ↔ 二 · A Person, and Two
subtitle: Graphic structure
evidence: Mojidata IDS: 仁 is 亻 beside 二. The Shuowen: 仁，親也。从人从二 — “closeness: from person and two.” The virtue is drawn as a relation.
caveat: Some scholars take 二 here as a mark rather than the numeral; the Shuowen’s “person and two” is the traditional reading.

label: 言 in 信
title: 信 ↔ 言 · A Person Standing by Their Word
subtitle: Graphic structure
evidence: Mojidata IDS: 信 is 亻 beside 言. The Shuowen: 信，誠也。从人从言 — “sincerity: from person and word.”

label: 父慈子孝
title: 孝 ↔ 慈 · Kindness Down, Devotion Up
subtitle: Liji, Liyun
evidence: The Liyun chapter of the Liji lists the ten duties of people: 父慈、子孝、兄良、弟弟、夫義、婦聽、長惠、幼順、君仁、臣忠 — the father kind, the child devoted … the ruler humane, the minister loyal. 慈 runs down the generations, 孝 runs up.
caveat: The list encodes a hierarchy of its time; Rushi records the pairing, not the order of persons.

label: 心 in 忠
title: 忠 ↔ 心 · The Heart Under the Centre
subtitle: Graphic structure
evidence: Mojidata IDS: 忠 is 中 over 心. The Shuowen: 忠，敬也。从心，中聲 — the heart for meaning, 中 for sound. One more graph with 心 at its foot, like 慈 and 悲.
caveat: Reading 忠 as “a centred heart” takes the phonetic 中 as meaning; it is a popular gloss, not the Shuowen’s.

label: 忠恕
title: 忠 ↔ 道 · The Master’s Way Is One Thread
subtitle: Analects 4.15
evidence: Analects 4.15: the Master said his way had one thread through it; Zengzi explained, 夫子之道，忠恕而已矣 — “the Master’s way is wholeheartedness and fellow-feeling, nothing more.”

title: 道 ↔ 慈 · The First Treasure
evidence: Daodejing 67 names 慈 as the first of three treasures, alongside frugality and not putting oneself first. This connects the Way to care through 慈; it does not make 愛 a quotation from the verse.
label: 三寶 · 慈
subtitle: Daodejing ch. 67

title: 不 ↔ 無 · Negation in Context
evidence: 不 commonly negates a predicate; 無 can express absence or non-possession. In Analects 1.16, 不 negates knowing. In 1.8, 無友 is a prohibition (“do not befriend”), showing why the simple gloss “無 = none” is not a rule for every sentence.
caveat: An introductory contrast illustrated by specific sentences, not an exhaustive grammar of Classical Chinese.
label: 不 · 無
subtitle: Absence, predication and prohibition
